label: Sumerian period
description: The Sumerian period. The gods An, Enlil, Enki, Nanna, Utu, and Inanna are worshipped. The great temples at Nippur (Enlil), Eridu (Enki), Ur (Nanna), and Uruk (Inanna) are built. The evidence is archaeological and cuneiform (Sumerian texts).

label: Akkadian period
description: The Akkadian period. The Sumerian gods are assimilated into the Akkadian pantheon (An becomes Anu, Enki becomes Ea, Nanna becomes Sin, Utu becomes Shamash, Inanna becomes Ishtar). Enlil becomes the king of the gods.

label: Old Babylonian period
description: The Old Babylonian period. Marduk rises to be the king of the gods (as Babylon rises to power). The Atrahasis and the early flood-stories are composed.

label: Standard Babylonian period
description: The Standard Babylonian period. The Enuma Elish (in its standard form) and the Epic of Gilgamesh (in its Standard Babylonian version) are composed. Marduk is the supreme god.

label: Neo-Babylonian / Achaemenid period
description: The Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid (Persian) period. Marduk is the supreme god (Neo-Babylonian); under the Persians, his supremacy declines. The great temple at Babylon (the Esagila) is still a center of worship.
